headline: Worldpay lifts revenue, GAAP profit lags adjusted gains
summary_short: Global Payments reported Q2 FY2026 GAAP revenue of $3.32 billion, up 68.6% y/y on the Worldpay acquisition, with adjusted diluted EPS of $3.46 (+11.7% y/y) even as GAAP diluted EPS fell to $0.05 on acquisition- and divestiture-related charges.
summary_long: GAAP revenue rose 68.6% y/y to $3.32 billion (+11.8% q/q) as Worldpay volumes consolidated for a full quarter; Enterprise segment revenue jumped to $838M from $149M while Issuer Solutions revenue fell to zero post-divestiture. Adjusted net revenue grew 33.8% y/y to $3.16 billion (normalized growth ~4%). GAAP diluted EPS of $0.05 reflects ~$994M of acquisition-amortization, integration and discontinued-operations charges excluded from adjusted diluted EPS of $3.46 (+11.7% y/y). Cash fell to $5.41 billion from $8.34 billion at year-end on debt paydown; long-term debt was $22.5 billion. Management raised full-year 2026 normalized adjusted net revenue growth guidance to 4%-5% and adjusted EPS to $13.60-$13.80, reaffirming plans to return more than $2 billion of capital to shareholders.

GAAP figures this quarter are heavily distorted by two one-time items: the Worldpay acquisition (added scale across the Enterprise/Platforms segments, pushing reported revenue up 68.6% y/y) and the divestiture of the Issuer Solutions business (a $102.0M net-of-tax loss from discontinued operations this quarter, on top of a $1.79B six-month net loss driven largely by the same transaction). Management's own non-GAAP figures (adjusted net revenue $3.159B, adjusted diluted EPS $3.46) strip out acquisition-related amortization and integration/separation costs and are the metrics management guides to; GAAP diluted EPS of $0.05 is not comparable to the year-ago $0.99 on a like-for-like basis. Q1 FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS of -$6.59 (the q/q comparator) itself reflected a large charge tied to classifying Issuer Solutions as held-for-sale/discontinued, so a q/q GAAP EPS comparison would not be meaningful and is omitted from the KPI table.

drivers.explanation: Enterprise segment revenue rose to $838M from $149M as Worldpay volumes consolidated for a full quarter, while Issuer Solutions revenue fell to zero following its divestiture.

GAAP EPS fell y/y mainly on acquisition-related amortization, integration/separation costs, and a $102M discontinued-operations loss tied to the Issuer Solutions divestiture, all excluded from adjusted EPS.

Management raised full-year 2026 outlook to 4%-5% normalized constant-currency adjusted net revenue growth and $13.60-$13.80 adjusted EPS, while reaffirming the plan to return more than $2 billion of capital to shareholders in 2026 despite headwinds from the Middle East conflict on the travel portfolio.
